nodes.text: A local cafe sales log containing daily revenue and transaction counts for the last 90 business days.

nodes.citation: Local daily weather log for the same 90-day period
nodes.text: A local weather log identifying which business days were rainy during the sales-log period.
The sales log can show whether average revenue or transaction count differs between rainy and non-rainy days.
Rainy days in the sample appear to have higher average transaction counts than non-rainy days.
The rainy-day label comes from the local weather log for the same period.
Rainy days bring more people into cafes because customers want an indoor place to wait or work.
component_claims: Customers choose cafes as indoor waiting or work spaces

nodes.text: The cafe sales log may be compatible with the rainy-day sales narrative, but it does not directly show why customers came in.
Rainy days may increase this cafe's sales, but the cause needs to be checked against confounders.
Rain may coincide with weekends, events, holidays, promotions, or seasonal changes.
nodes.why_risky: A simple rainy/non-rainy comparison may confuse weather with other sales drivers.
nodes.suggested_patch: Say 'may increase' and check day-of-week, events, promotions, and seasonality before making a stronger claim.

nodes.text: If the rainy-day effect disappears after controlling for weekends, events, promotions, and seasonality, UC1 is weakened.
nodes.required_evidence: A comparison that controls for day-of-week, special events, promotions, and seasonal period.
